page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.medium is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the ecs.m1 family, virtualized via the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a single thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is not enabled. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core.

This instance does not include local storage, requiring external block storage volumes for data persistence. There are no integrated GPUs. A key technical limitation of the underlying CPU is the absence of modern instruction set extensions; flags for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), cryptographic acceleration (AES, SHA_NI), and bit manipulation (BMI2, FMA) are unavailable.

Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is classified as general purpose. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without resource sharing, though the lack of advanced instruction sets limits its efficiency for specialized vector math, cryptography, or machine learning workloads. It is configured for standard general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, or application hosting that do not require local NVMe storage or hardware acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with a single thread per core, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance does not feature local storage or GPU accelerators, and it lacks advanced CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX, and AES cryptographic acceleration. Consequently, it is designed for standard computing tasks rather than high-performance vector processing or cryptography. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance for general-purpose workloads, including basic web serving, application hosting, and lightweight database tasks that rely on external block storage.
